title: Mohar's Conjecture
statement_text: For $k \geq 3$, all $k$-colourings of a $k$-regular graph that is not complete are Kempe equivalent.
context_text: Mohar conjectured in 2007 that for every connected non-complete $k$-regular graph with $k \geq 3$, the set of $k$-colourings forms a single Kempe class. The first non-trivial case $k=3$ was partially resolved: van den Heuvel found a counterexample (the triangular prism), and Feghali et al. showed it is the only one for $k=3$. This paper addresses the conjecture for all $k \geq 4$.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture for all $k \geq 4$: if $G$ is a connected non-complete $k$-regular graph with $k \geq 4$, then the set of $k$-colourings of $G$ is a Kempe class (Theorem 1.1).
paper_title: On a conjecture of Mohar concerning Kempe equivalence of regular graphs

title: Open case: WSK algorithm on the triangular lattice for q=5
statement_text: Determine whether the Wang-Swendsen-Koteck\'{y} algorithm for $q = 5$ colourings of the triangular lattice (with periodic boundary conditions) is valid (i.e., whether the set of $5$-colourings of the triangular lattice is a Kempe class).
context_text: For a proper colouring $\alpha$ and colours $a,b$, a Kempe chain is a connected component of the subgraph induced by the vertices coloured $a$ or $b$; a Kempe change swaps $a$ and $b$ on one Kempe chain. Two colourings are Kempe equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of Kempe changes, and a set of mutually Kempe equivalent colourings is a Kempe class. A triangular lattice with periodic boundary conditions is obtained from a toroidal grid (Cartesian product of two cycles) by adding one diagonal edge in each face, all diagonals parallel; it is a 6-regular triangulation of the torus. The Wang–Swendsen–Kotecký (WSK) algorithm is a Markov chain Monte Carlo cluster dynamics for the antiferromagnetic $q$-state Potts model; at zero temperature the configurations are the proper $q$-colourings, and the algorithm is valid (ergodic) exactly when the set of all $q$-colourings is a Kempe class. The paper proves Mohar's conjecture for $k\ge4$: every connected non-complete $k$-regular graph has all its $k$-colourings in one Kempe class (for $k=3$ the triangular prism is the only exception). Hence WSK is valid on the triangular lattice for $q=6$, and for $q\ge7$ because all $k$-colourings of a $d$-degenerate graph form a Kempe class when $k\ge d+1$; Mohar and Salas showed it is not valid for $q\le4$. Similarly WSK is valid on the Kagomé lattice iff $q\ge4$. This leaves $q=5$ on the triangular lattice, where neither argument applies (5 colours are fewer than the degree 6).
notes: Stated as an observation ('We observe that this leaves the single open case of a triangular lattice with q = 5') rather than in a formal labelled environment.
paper_title: On a conjecture of Mohar concerning Kempe equivalence of regular graphs
